import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/coffee_sales.csv')

# --- Data Preparation ---
# Combine 'date' and 'time' and convert to datetime objects
df['datetime'] = pd.to_datetime(df['date'] + ' ' + df['time'])

# Extract the hour of the day
df['hour'] = df['datetime'].dt.hour

# Group data by hour and product to calculate total sales
hourly_sales = df.groupby(['hour', 'product'])['total'].sum().reset_index()

# Find the top 5 products by total sales to keep the visualization clean
top_products = df.groupby('product')['total'].sum().nlargest(5).index
hourly_sales_top5 = hourly_sales[hourly_sales['product'].isin(top_products)]

# --- Visualization ---
# Set the aesthetic style of the plots
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid", palette="viridis")

# Create the figure and axes
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(14, 8))

# Create the line plot
sns.lineplot(
    data=hourly_sales_top5,
    x='hour',
    y='total',
    hue='product',
    style='product',
    markers=True,
    dashes=False,
    linewidth=2.5,
    ax=ax
)

# --- Customization and Labeling ---
# Set title and labels with enhanced formatting
ax.set_title('Peak Sales Hours for Top 5 Coffee Products', fontsize=18, fontweight='bold', pad=20)
ax.set_xlabel('Hour of the Day (24-hour format)', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax.set_ylabel('Total Sales ($)', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')

# Set x-axis ticks to be every hour for clarity
ax.set_xticks(range(0, 24, 1))
ax.set_xticklabels([f'{h:02d}:00' for h in range(24)], rotation=45, ha='right')
ax.grid(which='major', linestyle='--', linewidth='0.5', color='gray')

# Customize the legend
legend = ax.legend(title='Top Products', title_fontsize='13', fontsize='11')

# Add a text annotation for an insight
ax.text(8, hourly_sales_top5['total'].max() * 0.9, 'Morning rush peak',
        fontsize=12, style='italic', color='black',
        bbox=dict(facecolor='wheat', alpha=0.5, boxstyle='round,pad=0.5'))

# Final layout adjustment
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the final figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
